msg: DESCRIPTION Title must not end in a period. CRAN's Writing R Extensions: the Title is a short phrase in title case, no trailing full stop.
DESCRIPTION Title must be in title case. Capitalise every word except articles, conjunctions and short prepositions.
DESCRIPTION Description must not start with the package name, 'This package', 'A package' or 'The package'. Start with a verb or the subject itself.
DESCRIPTION Description must be at least one complete sentence that explains what the package does; a one-line restatement of the Title is rejected.
DESCRIPTION License is not a CRAN-accepted specification. Bare 'MIT', 'BSD' or an SPDX id is refused: use 'MIT + file LICENSE' with a two-line LICENSE file, or a standard spec such as 'GPL-3'.
DESCRIPTION must name exactly one maintainer: Authors@R needs one person() carrying role "cre" (or a Maintainer: field with a real address).
DESCRIPTION Version looks like a development version. CRAN refuses four-component and .9000 versions; submit a released three-part version.
DESCRIPTION carries a placeholder maintainer address. CRAN mails the submission confirmation to that address, so an example.com or template address ends the submission.
DESCRIPTION Date field is in the future or more than 31 days old; R CMD check --as-cran raises a NOTE for both. Drop the Date field or set it on the day you submit.
DESCRIPTION lists packages under Depends. Only 'R (>= x.y)' belongs there; packages you call belong in Imports plus importFrom() in NAMESPACE.
NAMESPACE uses exportPattern(), which exports internal objects too. CRAN expects every exported object to be documented; list export() entries instead.
library()/require() inside package code. CRAN policy: package code must not attach packages; declare the dependency in Imports and call it with pkg::fun() or importFrom().
The package tries to install software. CRAN policy: packages must not attempt to install other packages or write outside their own space.
setwd() changes the user's working directory. CRAN policy forbids changing the user's session state; build paths with file.path() instead.
options(), par() or Sys.setenv() is changed and never restored. CRAN policy: save the old value and put it back with on.exit(), e.g. oldpar <- par(no.readonly = TRUE); on.exit(par(oldpar)).
The package writes to the user's file space or a hard-coded path. CRAN policy: write only to tempdir(), and only inside the session.
T and F used for TRUE and FALSE. They are ordinary variables a user can rebind; R CMD check flags them and reviewers ask for the spelled-out constants.
print() or cat() writes to the console unconditionally. CRAN asks for message() or warning() so the user can suppress it; use print() only inside a print method.
\dontrun{} in an example. CRAN accepts it only when the example truly cannot run; if it is merely slow use \donttest{}, and expect to be asked why.
Non-ASCII character in R source. R CMD check --as-cran warns unless it is escaped as \uxxxx; portable packages keep source ASCII-only.
The package writes to the global environment. CRAN policy: packages must not modify the user's workspace, options, graphics devices or search path.
installed.packages() scans every library tree and is slow and unreliable. Use requireNamespace("pkg", quietly = TRUE) to test for a package.
set.seed() inside package code overwrites the user's random stream. CRAN asks that a seed be an argument the caller sets, not something a function fixes.
::: reaches into another package's internals. CRAN policy: do not use ::: to access undocumented objects in other packages, they may change without notice.
source() at package level. Package code is installed and lazy-loaded; sourcing files at run time breaks installed packages and byte-compilation.
